lead: Technology expands human capability, but every new layer of convenience also creates a new layer of dependence. In a digital environment, the scarce resource is no longer access to information but control over attention.

sections.heading: Technology as an amplifier
paragraphs: Technology has always extended human capability. Stone strengthened the hand. Machines multiplied physical productivity. Computers accelerated information work. The internet removed a large part of geographic limitation.
Artificial intelligence takes the next step by amplifying cognitive work: analysis, writing, information processing and the automation of intellectual tasks.

One person can now complete work that once required a team. A small group can operate in a global market. An idea can reach millions without traditional infrastructure. But every amplifier has two sides.

sections.heading: Information is no longer the scarce resource
paragraphs: Information used to be difficult to obtain. Access required a library, a specialist, a document or a person who possessed the relevant knowledge. Today the problem is the opposite: there is too much information.

News, messages, video, comments, advertising, recommendations, work channels and generative systems create a continuous flow. A person can spend an entire day in a digital environment, process hundreds of signals and still discover that almost nothing moved their own goals forward.
The advantage is therefore no longer access but filtering: separating signal from noise, the important from the loud, and useful information from content designed mainly to capture attention.

sections.heading: Attention became an economic resource
paragraphs: Many digital platforms make money when people remain inside them. Attention has economic value. This is why feeds are endless, notifications are persistent, recommendations are personalised and interfaces are constantly tested to keep the user engaged a little longer.
An algorithm does not need a political or moral goal. Optimising engagement is enough. Yet the human result can be the same: parts of behaviour gradually adapt to the logic of the platform.

Personalised systems make this more subtle. They can choose the message, format and timing for a specific person. Choice does not disappear, but the environment in which choice happens is increasingly designed rather than neutral.

sections.heading: From tool to environment
paragraphs: There is a fundamental difference between a hammer and a smartphone. A hammer stays on the table until it is needed. Digital technology is present continuously and has become part of the ordinary environment.
People communicate, work, receive money, study, navigate, store documents, buy goods and consume information through digital systems. Technology is no longer merely a separate tool.

The deeper the integration, the more expensive it becomes to function outside it. It is possible to reject a smartphone, but large parts of social and economic infrastructure immediately become harder to access. Autonomy can therefore shrink without any formal prohibition, simply because the cost of opting out keeps rising.

sections.heading: Rejecting technology is a weak response
paragraphs: When a tool genuinely expands capability, ignoring it often means simply falling behind. Artificial intelligence already automates parts of work, accelerates analysis and produces results with less time and effort.

The real question is not whether to use technology but what position to take toward it. Who decides when it is used? Who controls the information flow? Who decides which tasks are delegated to an algorithm and which abilities remain personal?
Technology in the hands of a person without control can become a source of distraction and dependence. The same technology in the hands of someone with clear goals can multiply results.

sections.heading: Autonomy does not mean going backwards
paragraphs: There is no need to reject navigation, artificial intelligence or digital payments in order to prove independence. It does make sense, however, to avoid letting the abilities replaced by systems disappear completely.

Think independently before searching for a ready-made answer. Know how to work without one specific platform. Preserve the ability to concentrate without constant stimulation. Understand the basic mechanics of tools on which work or daily life depends.
Dependence without an alternative creates vulnerability. Autonomy is not withdrawal from the modern world; it is the ability to use its tools without losing one’s own goals, attention and direction.

sections.heading: Two outcomes from the same technology
paragraphs: Technological development will not stop. Systems will become stronger, information will increase and artificial intelligence will take over more functions.
For one person this will mean an unprecedented expansion of possibility. For another it will mean deeper dependence, fragmented attention and less control over personal direction.
The tools may be identical. The difference will be determined by who keeps control of attention, decisions and goals in the relationship between person and system.
